record.paper_title: Mathematical contributions to the dynamics of the Josephson junctions: state of the art and open problems
record.context_brief: Interface conditions for window Josephson junctions
record.original_question: Can the perturbed sine-Gordon equation ε u_xxt + u_xx − u_tt − a u_t = sin(u) − γ be studied with interface conditions imposed on the phase u(x,t) and on its normal gradient, in order to model window Josephson junctions under the influence of an external magnetic field? Here u(x,t) is the phase difference between the wave functions of the two superconductors, ε u_xxt and a u_t represent longitudinal and shunt losses, and γ is the normalized current bias. The open problem is to formulate and analyze the resulting interface problem for the phase dynamics of such window Josephson junctions.

evidence.quote: The flux-dynamics of a Josephson junction, i.e, two layers of superconductors separated by a very thin layer of insulating material, can be described by means of Sine Gordon equation (SGE): (1.1) uxx − utt = sin u where x denotes the direction of propagation, t is time and the variable u = u(x, t) represents the difference between the phases of the wave functions of the two superconductors.

Therefore, many authors prefer to consider the so-called perturbed sine Gordon equation (PSGE): (1.2) εuxxt + uxx − utt − aut = sin u − γ. In this case, terms εuxxt and aut represent respectively the dissipative normal electron current flow along and across the junction, (longitudinal and shunt losses) while γ is the normalized current bias [2].

It would be interesting, for example, to study equation (1.2) when interface conditions for the phase (and its normal gradient) are added, connecting, in this way, with the problems of window Josephson junctions (WJJ) when the influence of an external magnetic field must be considered [52].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed sine-Gordon equation

    ε u_{xxt}(x,t) + u_{xx}(x,t) − u_{tt}(x,t) − a u_t(x,t) = sin(u(x,t)) − γ,

where u(x,t) ∈ ℝ represents the phase difference between the wave functions of two superconductors separated by a thin insulating layer, ε > 0 and a > 0 are dissipation parameters modeling, respectively, longitudinal (surface) losses and shunt (in-line) losses across the junction, and γ ∈ ℝ is a normalized constant current bias.

Let the spatial domain be a bounded interval (or, more generally, a one-dimensional region) Ω = (−L, L) ⊂ ℝ partitioned into a finite collection of open subintervals Ω₁, …, Ω_N separated by interface points {x_1, …, x_{N−1}} ⊂ Ω. On each subdomain Ω_k the equation above holds, possibly with subdomain-dependent coefficients (ε_k, a_k, γ_k) modeling alternating "window" and "passive" regions of a window Josephson junction. At each interface point x_j impose interface (transmission) conditions of the form

    [u]_{x_j} := u(x_j^+, t) − u(x_j^−, t) = 0,
    [β u_x]_{x_j} := β(x_j^+) u_x(x_j^+, t) − β(x_j^−) u_x(x_j^−, t) = h_j(t),

where β(x) > 0 is a piecewise constant coefficient (encoding the differing junction characteristics on the two sides of the interface) and h_j(t) accounts for the action of an external magnetic field at the interface. Boundary conditions of the form u_x(±L, t) = H_±(t) (Neumann data corresponding to an applied magnetic field) and initial conditions u(x,0) = u_0(x), u_t(x,0) = u_1(x) are prescribed.

Formulate this initial-boundary-value problem with interface conditions rigorously and analyze it: in particular, establish existence, uniqueness, regularity, and continuous dependence on the data (ε, a, γ, β, h_j, H_±, u_0, u_1) of a solution u, and study the long-time qualitative behavior (e.g., stability of equilibria, propagation of fluxons across the interfaces) of the resulting phase dynamics.
